  "type": "sector",

  "published": "2026-10-02",
  "insights": [
   "The Federal Reserve released final CCAR stress test rules on 9/30/26, largely in line with prior proposals, alongside a new NPR on PPNR.",
   "Key changes include two-year averaging of stress capital declines (effective 2028), a shift in the SCB effective date to January 1, and a dual Global Market Shock (GMS) framework.",
   "The Fed introduced a mandatory public notice-and-comment process for stress models and scenarios, increasing transparency.",
   "Goldman Sachs estimates the final rules will have a largely neutral impact on excess capital for the top 7 banks, with total excess capital remaining at $78bn.",
   "The firm expects a modest ~5bps increase in top 7 banks' SCBs if using 2025-26 averages, with minimal impact on EPS and a slight ~5bps ROTCE downside.",
   "The new NPR on noninterest fee income aims to differentiate between stable contractual fee streams and volatile transactional revenue for the 2027 cycle.",
   "The Fed implemented guardrails to limit intrayear volatility, such as bounds on 5Y UST rate movements in stress scenarios.",
   "Liquidity horizons for asset class shocks are being reduced to be consistent with Basel 3 Endgame standards, resulting in 1-3 month horizons."
